message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic chills, modern scares, and psychological thrills—perfect for a Friday‑night binge:

| # | Title & Year | Director / Key Cast | Why It Works |
|---|---------------|---------------------|--------------|
| **1** | *Halloween* (1978) – John Carpenter | Classic slasher vibe, iconic score, unforgettable villain Michael Myers. Great for building tension slowly before the big reveal. |
| **2** | *Hereditary* (2018) – Ari Aster | Psychological dread + supernatural family curse. Intense atmosphere and unsettling performances make this one truly unnerving. |
| **3** | *Get Out* (2017) – Jordan Peele | Horror meets social satire. Clever twists and creepy pacing keep you guessing until the end. |
| **4** | *A Quiet Place* (2018) – John Krasinski | Silence as weapon. Tension builds through sound design alone—a fresh take on creature feature logic. |
| **5** | *It Follows* (2014) – David Robert Mitchell | Modern folklore twist: an invisible entity stalks its victims at a constant pace. Creepy soundtrack amplifies paranoia. |
| **6** | *Midsommar* (2019) – Ari Aster | Daylight horror! Bright Swedish summer turns into a cult nightmare—visual feast plus disturbing rituals. |
| **7** | *The Conjuring* (2013) – James Wan | Paranormal investigation turned terrifying. Strong characters, effective jump‑scares, and atmospheric creepiness. |
| **8** | *Suspiria* (1977) – Dario Argento | Giallo masterpiece. Colorful visuals, haunting piano score, and a dance academy full of secrets. |
| **9** | *Paranorman* (2009) – Sam Fell & Chris Butler | Animated horror‑comedy. Fun yet genuinely spooky, great for lighter fright without losing depth. |
| **10** | *Us* (2019) – Jordan Peele | Mirror image terror. Duality theme, strong ensemble cast, and a chilling climax that stays with you long after the credits roll. |

Feel free to pick based on your mood—whether you want slow‑burn dread (*Hereditary*, *Midsommar*) or fast‑paced jumpscares (*Halloween*, *The Conjuring*). Enjoy the scare fest!
